item.title: DDS2 Endgame Guide: What to Do After Maxing Everything
item.description:
Once you have maxed out your Street Cred, staffed all roles, unlocked every recipe, and built hideouts across all islands, what is left to do in DDS2? The endgame offers several directions: achievement hunting, Casino DLC content, co-op challenges, and self-imposed goals. This guide covers everything available after the main progression is complete.

item.title: DDS2 Map and Island Guide: All Locations, POIs, and Fast Travel Routes
item.description:
Isla Sombra in DDS2 consists of multiple islands, each with its own characteristics, client base, police density, and available resources. Understanding the map layout is essential for efficient travel, territory planning, and supply chain management. This guide covers every accessible island, key points of interest, and the fastest travel routes between them.

Island overview:

Based on the community maps on Miraheze and Kanka, there are 7 major island zones:

Island Unlock Order Best For Police Density
Small Island Starting zone Tutorial, early deliveries, no police None
Archipelago First expansion General operations, restaurant district Low
Callejon Mid-game Processing, industrial equipment, gang territory Medium
Jungle Mid-game Cannabis growing, raw materials Low
Slavs Bay Late-game High-end production (meth, cocaine) High
Paraiso Peninsular Late-game Endgame operations, high-value clients High
Bahia De Oro Endgame Casino DLC area, premium clients Very High

The islands are gated by Street Cred level and story progression. You cannot access Callejon until you have completed sufficient missions in Archipelago. Similarly, Slavs Bay and later areas require higher Street Cred.

item.title: DDS2 Reputation Guide: Street Cred Leveling and Fast Strategies
item.description:
The reputation system in DDS2, called "Street Cred," controls what you can unlock. Higher Street Cred levels unlock better recipes, larger hideout upgrades, more staff slots, higher-value customer tiers, and access to restricted areas. The achievement "I Am The One Who Knocks" requires Street Cred level 4. This guide covers how the system works and the fastest ways to level up.

How Street Cred works:

Street Cred is separate from your wanted level. Wanted level is police heat that decays with time. Street Cred is your reputation in the criminal underworld that permanently increases. You cannot lose Street Cred through normal gameplay -- only arrests can potentially reduce it. The system has multiple levels, and each level requires more experience than the last.

item.title: DDS2 Vehicle and Boat Guide: Best Purchases, Upgrades, and Customization
item.description:
Vehicles in DDS2 are essential for efficient travel between islands. The starter boat is slow and has limited fuel capacity. Upgrading to faster vehicles with larger fuel tanks dramatically improves your delivery speed and territory reach. Based on community guides from Steam and the Miraheze wiki, this guide covers all vehicles, their stats, prices, and which to buy at each stage.

Why vehicles matter:

Walking between islands takes 15-30 minutes each way. A basic boat cuts this to 5 minutes. A car or upgraded boat can cross the map in 2-3 minutes. Time saved on travel is time spent on production and sales. The right vehicle choice can increase your effective income by 50% or more.

item.description:

Use Completionist mode for achievement hunting. It removes quota pressure and gives unlimited time. In Standard mode, quota deadlines interrupt focused achievement runs. Switch modes from the main menu before starting a new game.

item.title: DDS2 Meth Recipe: Cook Your First Batch (Step-by-Step)
item.description:
The DDS2 Datamine v2 catalogs 73 substances. Meth starts at POT 0.88 (pure potency). The first cook is straightforward once you know the ingredient chain: ephedrine to compound to purify to cut. I wasted my first few batches guessing ratios. This guide walks through every step from ingredient sourcing to finished product.

Step 1: Unlock the recipe

Before you can cook meth, you need the recipe. The recipe card is a physical item found in the tutorial zone warehouse. Unlike some games where recipes auto-unlock, DDS2 requires you to find the card and interact with it. The recipe unlocks as part of the main story questline -- you will receive a prompt to find it after talking to your contact about making more money.

item.description:
Employees in DDS2 are essential for scaling past the early game. I spent my first 20 hours running everything solo before realizing how much time staff saves. item.title: DDS2 Parkour Guide: Movement Mechanics and Police Escape
item.description: The DDS2 Fandom tutorial page confirms: "Use parkour to find shortcuts, to make it easier to escape from enemies chasing you, or to sneak into otherwise inaccessible areas." Parkour is your primary survival tool -- not guns. I stopped trying to fight police after my first few arrests taught me that bullets attract more heat than they solve. This guide covers every parkour move, when to use each, and how to chain them into effective escape sequences.

item.title: DDS2 Hideout Locations Guide and Raid Protection
item.description: Hideouts in DDS2 are your operational bases, and they can be raided based on your wanted level and the hideout's visibility rating. I lost my first major stockpile to a raid because I kept everything in the starter shack. The community guide "Pedro Alvarez Real Estate Agency" documents all locations with prices, water/phone line availability, and visibility ratings. This guide covers how to choose hideouts, how raids work, and how to protect your assets.

item.title: Best Early-Game Money Methods in DDS2 (Verified)
item.description:
The fastest early-game money in DDS2 comes from delivery grinding and territory expansion, not cooking. I tried going straight to cooking and ended up broke with wasted materials. In the first 10 hours, deliveries outperform cooking by roughly 3:1 based on what I have seen and what the community confirms. This guide covers the three phases of early money-making, from zero to a sustainable operation.

item.title: DDS2 Beginner's Guide: From Beach to First $5K
item.description: Your first hour on Isla Sombra is about survival, not profits. I learned this the hard way -- my first run I focused on cooking and ended up broke with no clients. Complete the tutorial missions, meet your contact Shady, secure your first hideout, and make deliveries until you hit $5,000. Cooking comes after you have a reliable client pipeline. This guide walks through every step from washing up on the beach to building a sustainable early-game operation.

item.title: Crime Simulator 4-Player Co-op Strategy Guide
item.description:
I played most of Crime Simulator solo before trying co-op. The difference is night and day -- with a coordinated team, you clear houses faster and pull in way more loot per run. But without coordination, co-op is chaos.

The Optimal Role Setup

The fastest role setup I have used: 1 Lockpick + 1 Lookout + 1 Hauler + 1 Driver. Rotate roles every 2-3 runs so everyone stays flexible.

item.title: Crime Simulator Fast Money Guide: Best Early-Game Methods
item.description:
The fastest first $1,000 I found: complete the tutorial, grab the crowbar, rob the nearest low-security house, sell electronics at the fence, buy a lockpick set. Repeat with better entry on house number two. Took me about 20 minutes of real time.

The early game is about capital accumulation. Every dollar goes back into tools that enable better heists. I wasted my first payout on hideout decorations and regretted it for the next hour.

item.title: Crime Simulator Hardcore Mode Survival Guide
item.description:
I lost my first Hardcore run in under 30 minutes. Broke a lockpick on my first door, panicked, used the crowbar, alerted a patrol, got chased, arrested, save gone. Not my finest moment.

Hardcore mode deletes your save on arrest. Quotas are higher (about 1.5x), police are more aggressive, and fence prices are approximately 20% lower. The core loop is the same but the margin for error is razor thin.

item.title: Crime Simulator Loot Locations and Item Values Guide
item.description:
Not all loot is worth the same inventory slot. I learned this the hard way after filling my bag with kitchen appliances worth $40 each while passing laptops worth $200+. Understanding what to grab and what to leave behind is the single biggest factor in beating quotas consistently.

Loot Value Tiers

Crime Simulator loot falls into three broad value tiers. Memorize these so you never waste a slot on low-value junk.

item.title: Crime Simulator Tools Guide: Every Item Explained
item.description:
I spent my first few Crime Simulator runs using nothing but the crowbar on every door. Loud, slow, and got me caught repeatedly. Better tools changed everything.

Prioritize the lockpick set first. It replaces the noisy crowbar on most locked doors and pays for itself within 2-3 heists.

Tool Overview

Crime Simulator has a growing arsenal of tools for breaking in, disabling security, and escaping. Tools break with use and must be repaired or replaced. Choosing the right tool for each job is the difference between a clean score and an arrest.

item.title: Getting Started in Crime Simulator
item.description:
I started Crime Simulator in debt with nothing but a crowbar and a hideout. Took me a few restarts to figure out the flow. Here is what I wish I knew from the start.

The tutorial teaches the basic loop: find a house, break in, steal stuff, sell it, repeat. It is short but do not skip the lockpicking practice -- I spent my first few real runs fumbling with it and getting caught because I rushed past that part.

item.title: Crime Simulator Game Modes and Quota System Explained
item.description:
Crime Simulator has three game modes. The differences are significant -- mode choice determines how punishing the quota is, whether you can die permanently, and how much time you have to explore. Pick the wrong mode and you will restart more than necessary.

Mode Comparison

Feature Standard Hardcore Completionist
Permadeath No Yes No
Difficulty Normal Master (locked) Variable
Quota Every 3 days Every 3 days No time limit
Quota penalty Warning, then demote Full reset None
Police aggression Normal +50% (community estimate) Normal
Fence prices 100% ~80% 100%
Final score bonus 1x 2x N/A
Best for Learning the game Challenge runs Achievements

Standard Mode

Standard is the recommended starting mode. Difficulty is set to Normal. Quotas appear every 3 in-game days with a minimum dollar target. Fail the quota and you get a warning. Fail again and your rank decreases. Fail repeatedly and the game ends.

item.title: Which Property to Buy First, Second, Third: The Order That Worked for Me
item.description:
I messed up my property order on my first playthrough. Bought the Warehouse before I had the cash flow to staff it. Wasted a lot of in-game days staring at empty shelves. Here's the order I settled on after restarting.

The buy order that makes sense:

Apartment (free) -> Bungalow ($6K at Hustler) -> Barn ($25K at Dealer) -> Docks Warehouse ($50K at Hoodlum V) -> Hyland Manor ($250K at Kingpin)

item.title: DDS2 Cutting Agents Guide: Maximize Profit Without Killing Customers
item.description:
The DDS2 Datamine v2 reveals that cutting agents have three key properties: TOX (toxicity), POT (potency multiplier), and ADD (addiction). Use low-TOX agents like flour and sugar to double volume without losing customers. I tested several cutting ratios and the difference in customer retention is dramatic -- switching from high-TOX to low-TOX agents turned my business around from losing customers to steady repeat orders.

How cutting agents work:

Each cutting agent modifies the final product's stats when mixed in. The goal is to maximize volume (by adding cheap filler) while keeping toxicity low enough that customers survive to re-order.

item.description:
Getting raided in DDS2 is preventable. I know because I have been raided several times and each time I could trace it back to something I did wrong. The game's raid system checks wanted level and hideout visibility. Keep both low and your assets stay safe. This guide covers the mechanics behind raids, prevention strategies, and what to do when a raid happens anyway.

item.title: DDS2 Late-Game Empire: Scaling with Employees and Multi-Hideout Strategy
item.description:
Scaling past $50,000 in DDS2 requires employees, multiple specialized hideouts, and territory control. The Reddit community organizes by product type -- one hideout for cannabis, one for amphetamine, one for meth. I use this approach and it scales reliably. This guide covers how to transition from a solo operator to a full cartel with automated income streams.

Employee system:

Employees are unlocked through notice boards (random spawn at bulletin board locations across islands), influencer missions (limited uses per influencer -- typically 2 hires each), and story progression. Once hired, employees can be assigned to different roles.

item.title: 10 DDS2 Tips the Game Doesn't Tell You (Serper Verified)
item.description:
The DDS2 tutorial covers basic controls but skips the survival mechanics that experienced players rely on. I picked these up from reading Steam community guides, Reddit discussions, and losing a few hideouts before I figured it out. These 10 tips will save you from the most common early-game mistakes.

1. Use multiple hideouts early.

Hideout raid risk is affected by wanted level and visibility. The Fandom wiki confirms helicopters can appear during raids and you can lose stored assets. I split raw materials, finished product, and cash across 3+ hideouts now. Never keep everything in one location. The ideal split: one hideout for raw materials, one for processing equipment, one for finished product. If any single hideout gets raided, you lose at most one-third of your operation.

item.title: Crime Simulator Achievement Guide Part 2: Hard Achievements
item.description:
These are the achievements that took me real effort to unlock. Some require multiple playthroughs or very specific conditions. I would not attempt them until you have completed Standard mode and understand all the mechanics.

Challenge Achievements (15)

Challenges are optional objectives that appear during runs. Completing them in specific quantities unlocks these achievements.

Achievement Requirement Difficulty Strategy
Insane victory Complete 5 challenges in one game Medium Pick a medium house with multiple challenge types
Master challenger Complete 10 challenges in one game Hard Requires a large multi-room house
Challenge addict Complete 25 challenges total Medium Grind across multiple runs
Speed demon Complete 3 time-based challenges Hard Small apartment, clear rooms fast
Silent but deadly Complete 3 stealth challenges Medium Use silenced tools only
Heavy hitter Complete 3 destruction challenges Medium Break doors, windows, containers
All-rounder Complete one of each challenge type Very Hard Plan route for stealth + destruction + speed

For "All-rounder," I used a large house with multiple approaches. Ground floor for stealth, basement for destruction, upstairs for time-based tasks. One house can satisfy all challenge types if you plan your route.

item.title: Crime Simulator Co-op Heist Planning: From Setup to Extraction
item.description:
The best co-op heists I have been on were planned before anyone left the hideout. The team I run with spends 5 minutes planning and 10 minutes executing. Those 5 minutes save us from 20 minutes of prison time.

Pre-Heist Briefing Checklist

Before leaving the hideout, we confirm every item on this list:

  • Target selected from job board or free-roam
  • Security level assessed (locks, NPCs, alarms)
  • Required tools confirmed for each team member
  • Entry point identified (front, back, roof, window)
  • Extraction point agreed (vehicle, alley, rooftop)
  • Role assignments confirmed
  • Communication channel set (in-game voice or Discord)
  • Hard extraction limit agreed (time limit for aborting)
Assign a team leader for each heist. One person makes the call to abort. If everyone has veto power, you get indecision. I have seen teams lose 15 minutes arguing over whether to push or pull. A single decision-maker prevents this.

Target Selection

Not all houses are worth hitting in co-op. The payout from a single large house split 4 ways is sometimes less than running two medium houses simultaneously.

item.title: Crime Simulator Gold Bars and Jewelry Economy (Update 1.3)
item.description:
Do not sell gold bars for quick cash. I made this mistake on my first 1.3 playthrough and regretted it when I realized gold bars are the currency for hideout basement upgrades -- and those upgrades unlock higher-value contracts that pay back 5x the gold's fence price.

What Changed in Update 1.3

Update 1.3 introduced a parallel economy system that fundamentally changes how you should think about loot:

  • Gold bars -- new resource for hideout basement upgrades
  • Jewelry loot -- authentic and fake variants with different values
  • Basement hideout expansion -- upgradeable with gold bars
  • PvP competition modes -- new income stream with risk
  • Master Key -- premium tool for instant lock opening
  • New loot locations with expanded map areas

Gold Bars: The Basement Currency

Found in high-security targets, heist locations, and rare loot boxes. Gold bars are heavy and take multiple inventory slots. They are used exclusively for basement upgrades.

item.title: Crime Simulator Hardcore Mode Progression: From Zero to Rank 6+
item.description:
This assumes you have read the Hardcore Survival Guide first. If you have not completed a single Hardcore heist yet, start there. This covers the longer arc from first heist to endgame mastery.

Phase 1: The First Heist (Rank Apprentice)

Your first Hardcore heist is the most dangerous because you have zero tools and zero skill leaves. I accept the lowest-risk house from the job board, enter through a window (quieter than crowbar on a door), grab only 3-4 visible items, exit within 60 seconds, and sell everything immediately.

item.title: Crime Simulator Loot Selling Strategy: Maximize Every Heist
item.description:
Most new players sell every item they find to the nearest fence immediately. I did this for my first few hours and left a lot of money on the table.

The fastest way from zero to quota (what I settled on): stack item requests, sell duplicate skill leaflets before basic loot, and never fence high-value items at the same fence twice in one day -- prices drop.

The Four Rules of Loot Selling

Rule 1: Item Requests First

The item request system offers 50-100% premium over fence prices. Before selling anything, I check the request board, mark requested items, and keep them in stash. Deliver on the next visit to that map area.

item.title: Crime Simulator Tool Upgrades and Advanced Tools
item.description:
Basic tools get the job done, but upgraded versions save time, reduce noise, and fail less often. I went from breaking a lockpick every 2-3 heists to going 10+ on the professional set.

The Master Key from Update 1.3 is the best late-game tool investment I have unlocked. It opens most standard locks instantly, dramatically speeding up heists.

Tool Quality Tiers

Each tool type has multiple quality tiers. Higher tiers are more expensive but break less often and work faster.

item.title: Crime Simulator Common Mistakes: 10 Critical Errors New Players Make
item.description:
I made every mistake on this list during my first few hours of Crime Simulator. Some cost me a single heist. Others cost me entire Hardcore runs. Here is what I learned so you do not have to learn it the same way.

Mistake 1: Selling Gold Bars for Quick Cash

This is the single most expensive mistake new players make. Gold bars are not loot -- they are currency for basement upgrades. Selling a gold bar for $800-$1,500 seems like great early-game money, but that same bar funds a Storage Rack upgrade that increases your stash capacity by 50%.

item.title: Crime Simulator Endless Mode Guide: Complete Strategy and Survival Tips
item.description:
Endless mode in Crime Simulator removes the quota timer and day limit, letting you progress at your own pace. Loot respawns daily in houses you have already cleared. This mode is perfect for learning the game, grinding achievements, and testing strategies without pressure.

How Endless Mode Works

Endless mode was added in Update 1.1. Key mechanics:

  • No quota deadlines -- quotas exist but never expire
  • Loot respawns daily -- houses reset with new loot every game day
  • Full progression -- ranks, tools, skills, and upgrades all carry over
  • Death penalty -- same as Standard mode (lose carried loot, keep rank/upgrades)
  • Police system -- police AI behaves the same as Standard mode
  • Difficulty selection -- choose Casual, Normal, Pro, or Master difficulty
Feature Endless Mode Standard Mode
Quota deadline None Every 3 days
Loot respawn Daily Per run
Map progression Unlock by rank Unlock by rank
Death penalty Lose carried loot Lose carried loot
Best for Learning, grinding Challenge runs

Why Play Endless Mode?

item.title: Crime Simulator House Tier Guide: Map Districts and Loot Value
item.description:
Crime Simulator has multiple districts, each with different house types, security levels, and loot potential. Knowing which district to target at each stage of the game saves you time and reduces risk.

District Overview

District Unlock Rank Difficulty Average Loot per House Police Response
Starter Town Apprentice Low $100-$300 45-60 seconds
Suburban Rank 3 Medium $300-$600 30-45 seconds
Industrial Rank 6 Medium-High $400-$800 60-90 seconds
Downtown Rank 10 High $600-$1,200 20-30 seconds
Heist Locations Rank 12+ Very High $1,000-$3,000 15-25 seconds

House Types by District

Starter Town (Rank Apprentice)

Small, single-story houses with minimal security. No electronic locks, few NPCs, low-value loot. Best for learning the basics.

item.title: Crime Simulator Police System Guide: AI Behavior and Evasion
item.description:
The police system in Crime Simulator is the primary fail state. Understanding exactly how it works -- what triggers it, how fast police respond, and how to evade them -- is the difference between a clean score and a deleted save in Hardcore mode.

How Police Detection Works

Police are triggered by a heat system. Every action you take generates heat. When your heat reaches a threshold, police are called.

item.title: Crime Simulator Safe Houses Guide: Best Hideouts and Upgrades
item.description:
Your hideout is more than just a place to store loot. It is your operations center, your safe zone, and the key to long-term progression. Choosing the right upgrades and managing your storage effectively can double your earning potential.

Hideout Basics

Your hideout serves several critical functions:

  • Storage: Keep loot between runs for item requests or bulk selling
  • Safe zone: Police cannot enter your hideout -- get here and you are safe
  • Save point: The game autosaves when you visit your hideout
  • Job board: Accept heist contracts and item requests
  • Upgrades: Basement expansion (Update 1.3) unlocks powerful bonuses

Storage Management

Your hideout has limited storage space. Managing it well is essential.

item.title: Crime Simulator Skill Leaflets Guide: Complete List and Priority Order
item.description:
Skill leaflets are the backbone of progression in Crime Simulator. Unlike tools that you buy with cash, skill leaflets must be found during heists and then activated with skill points earned from ranking up. Choosing the right leaflet priority can save you dozens of hours.

How Skill Leaflets Work

Each skill leaflet unlocks a permanent ability or upgrade. To activate a leaflet, you need:

  • The leaflet item (found during heists)
  • One skill point (earned by ranking up)

You can find duplicate leaflets. Once you have learned a skill, duplicate leaflets sell for approximately $300-$500 at the fence -- a decent income source, especially in the early game.

item.title: Bungalow Setup: My Layout After 3 Different Attempts
item.description:
The Bungalow ($6,000) was the first property where I actually felt like I was running a real operation. The apartment works fine for the first hour, but once you need more than 2 Mixing Stations and actual employees, you outgrow it fast.

I rebuilt the Bungalow layout three times before it clicked. Here's what worked and what didn't.

The layout that finally clicked:

The Bungalow is a single open room, about 8x6 tiles of usable space. No stairs, no extra rooms. You work with what you have.

item.title: Manual vs Automation ROI Comparison: Which Setup Makes Money Faster
item.description:
Short answer: Full automation (Barn + 10 employees) earns roughly 5x more per day than manual play, but costs ~$45,000 upfront with a 5-8 day break-even. Partial automation (Bungalow + 3 employees) is the best value: ~$3,500 setup, 7-10 day break-even. Manual play breaks even instantly but caps at ~$2,000/day earnings.

This guide is a data comparison -- not a setup tutorial. Use the table below to decide whether automation is worth it for your current stage.

item.title: Fastest Supplier Unlock Route: From Street Rat to Kingpin in Minimum Orders
item.description:
Short answer: Unlock Albert Hoover immediately (available from start). Befriend Elizabeth Homley or Kevin Oakley to unlock Shirley Watts and Fungal Phil simultaneously. Reach higher ranks for Salvador Moreno. The fastest route: place Dead Drop orders for the cheapest items first to build relationship, then scale up. Minimum total cost to unlock all four: roughly $8,000 in Dead Drop orders plus rank progression.

This is an optimized unlock route -- not a list of who the suppliers are. Follow this order and you'll unlock delivery (the max relationship perk) faster than random ordering.

item.title: 10 Common Mistakes Beginners Make in DDS2 (And How to Fix Them)
item.description:
Every DDS2 player makes mistakes in their first playthrough. I made most of these myself -- some cost me hours of progress. This guide covers the 10 most common beginner mistakes and how to avoid or recover from each one. Based on my own experience and community discussions from Reddit and Steam.

1. Keeping everything in one hideout.

The most common and most costly mistake. A single raid can wipe out your entire operation if everything is in one place. I lost my first major stockpile this way.

item.title: NPC Price Index 2026: Which Dealer Pays The Most Per Product Type
item.description:
Short answer: Leo Rivers pays the most per unit across all product types (up to 20% more than Benji Coleman for premium products). But the best deal in the game is assigning low-spending customers to dealers and selling directly to high-spenders. This guide ranks all 6 dealers by what they pay per product type, so you know exactly who should sell what.

This is not a "who the dealers are" explainer. This is a price index -- a ranked reference for maximizing per-unit profit through dealer assignment.

item.title: Police AI Behavior: Detection Distances, Chase Durations, and Best Hiding Spots
item.description:
Short answer: Police in Schedule I use line-of-sight (LOS) detection with a 15m base range. Detection is blocked by walls, vehicles, and terrain. Chase duration scales with heat level: 30s at Level 1, 60s at Level 2, 90s at Level 3, 3min+ at Level 4. Entering a safe house clears all heat instantly. The parking garage roof near the motel is the only 100% safe spot at all heat levels as of v0.4.5.

This breakdown shows you exactly how cops think, so you can exploit their AI patterns instead of running blindly.
